1.why: The single-column layout has no animations, images, or pop-ups, though the dense dark Logs console on every screen adds some visual clutter.

2.why: The highlighted current-step pill, bold headings, and solid teal primary buttons make the key element on each screen stand out clearly.

3.why: Each screen offers one labeled field and one primary action, but on steps 2 and 5 the user must locate the required code inside the busy Logs panel.

4.why: The persistent 5-step indicator and on-screen instructions carry the process, but the four-part password rule and the 64-character recovery code still tax working memory.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager option, or explicit autofill affordance appears on any of the seven screens.

6.why: The identical header, step pills, and persistent Logs panel keep previously seen items (steps, issued codes) visible so the user can recognize rather than recall them.

7.why: Instructions are short plain sentences (e.g., 'Take your time: this step will stay here until you are ready'), with only minor jargon like 'MFA' and the awkward 'simulated recovery delivery' phrasing.

8.why: No error state appears in any screenshot, so there is no evidence of whether error messages describe problems and fixes.

9.why: Password requirements are listed and the Logs panel shows the actual code to enter, but no concrete examples such as a sample password or field placeholders are provided.

10.why: No authentication choices exist: sign-in is password-only and MFA is code-only, with no face login or alternative methods shown.

11.why: Each screen presents at most one input and one or two buttons, so the user never faces more than a couple of choices at once.

12.why: Every action ends with an explicit outcome banner: 'Code verified', 'Password saved', 'Identity confirmed. You are signed in', and 'Privacy statement accepted'.

13.why: Every screen includes a 'Need help?' link plus short contextual tips such as 'We will guide you one step at a time' and 'Need another code? You may request one here'.

14.why: A 'Send a new recovery code' button, no session countdown, and gentle rate-limit wording support retrying, though recovery from wrong input is never shown.

15.why: All seven screens share the same header, step indicator, card layout, button styling, help link, and Logs panel, making the design highly consistent.
